name: Rasuwa flood
where: Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and downstream, Nepal
headline: Rasuwa flood, live
lede: A flash flood came down the Bhote Koshi from Tibet into Rasuwa on 26 August 2026. Here is what is confirmed, what is still unknown, and who to call.

stats.label: confirmed dead
stats.detail: Nepal Police reported 626 bodies found in Nepal by 2pm Saturday. Its district breakdown sums to 626: Chitwan 233, Nawalparasi East 158, Gorkha 54, Nawalparasi West 47, Dhading 49, Nuwakot 41, Tanahun 31 and Rasuwa 13. NDRRMA reported the same national total in its 10am Saturday update. China's separate toll of 7 is not added here.

stats.label: listed missing in Nepal
stats.detail: NDRRMA listed 2,426 people out of contact in Nepal in its 10am Saturday situation update, up from 1,924 in its Friday evening update. The authority's earlier category breakdown is not a breakdown of this new total. Out of contact does not mean dead: disrupted phones, power and internet can prevent contact. This is NDRRMA's figure, not Nepal Police's.

stats.label: missing on the China side
stats.detail: Xinhua, China's state news agency, reports 554 people missing around Gyirong Port in Xizang (Tibet) as of Saturday morning, down slightly from the 558 Chinese media had given earlier, with 260 of them foreign nationals. Combined with Nepal's list that is more than 2,400 people unaccounted for across both countries, although the two countries' counts of foreign nationals may overlap.

stats.label: rescued so far
stats.detail: NDRRMA reported 4,451 people rescued in its 10am Saturday situation update. Its earlier named nationality list totals 113, so it is not a full breakdown of the current total. Nepal Police had separately reported 2,301 rescued as of 7am Saturday. Agency totals can differ by reporting time and scope.

stats.label: hydropower projects damaged
stats.detail: The Nepal Electricity Authority reports 14 projects damaged with a combined capacity of about 748 MW: 9 operating plants (354 MW) and 5 under construction (394 MW). Named ones include Rasuwagadhi, Chilime, Sanjen Khola, Upper Trishuli-1, Trishuli and Devighat, plus a 220 kV substation. An earlier same-day Ministry of Energy estimate said 431 MW.

stats.label: since the flood
stats.detail: Counting from the morning of 26 August 2026, when the flood hit. Search, rescue and recovery work is still going on this many days later.

stats.label: damage, early estimate
stats.detail: Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal put damage to roads and bridges at about Rs 200 billion on 26 August, and called it preliminary. Hydropower and private property are not in that figure. The whole 42 km road from Betrawati to the Rasuwagadhi border crossing was destroyed at multiple points.

stats.label: relief money released
stats.detail: Rs 1 billion released by the government into the disaster relief fund, plus Rs 10 million each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Rs 5 million to Dhading. Public donations are not counted here until an official total is published.
